newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major pins hopes on undecided voters.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major pins hopes on undecided voters.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Tuesday said his Conservative Party could still win Thursday's election because a large number of people have not declared who they will vote for.
"I think there is a very large number of people, whether they have made their minds up or not, haven't declared what their mind is," Major told BBC radio.

"I think people will judge the government on the record over five years. Whatever measure you take -- inflation, unemployment, growth in living standards, competitiveness in industry -- the country is in far better shape," he said.
The latest opinion poll, from the Daily Telegraph newspaper and Gallup, gave Labour a 22 points lead. With one exception. polls over the last week have put Labour between 15 and 24 points ahead.
But even Labour leader Tony Blair has been at pains to play down the polls, saying he did not think there was talk of landslides out in the country.
"There is a real world beyond the opinion polls," Major added. He admitted his party was divided over the single European currency but said Labour was too.
"There has been one area and one area alone where there has been division. And that division exists...equally in the main opposition party," Major said.
There was no split in the Conservative Party over retaining vetos in the European Union, rejecting the EU's Social Chapter, or defying moves to more federalism, he said.
